evals.prompt: Which of my renewals in the next 90 days are at risk? I've dumped three exports in here — the CRM one has a couple of title rows above the header and the ARR column came through as text.
evals.expected_output: A ranked risk assessment over the renewal window: the files ingested without a re-export being requested, a bottom line with ARR at risk, a priority table ranked by Action Priority (not raw score), account cards for everything At Risk and above, all seven signal families reported including clean and missing ones, a Coverage Ledger with a confidence cap, and an Assumption Register for anything defaulted.
assertions: Runs the shared ingest step on the supplied files rather than asking the user to re-export or reformat them
Finds the real header row beneath the title rows and parses the text-formatted ARR column as money, confirming any column mapping below 0.80 confidence before scoring on it
Asks for and records the data as-of date rather than treating the export as current
Computes and uses the opt-out deadline (renewal_date minus notice_period_days), not the renewal date alone
Ranks by ARR-weighted exposure times urgency times savability, with the arithmetic shown, not by raw score
Reports all seven signal families for each account, including families that came back clean, and ends with a Coverage Ledger with a coverage percentage and a stated confidence cap
Ends with an Assumption Register table whose every row names a concrete consequence, not 'may affect results'

Prints the four required reads on every account card — the calendar three-tuple (C22), negotiation friction (C24), the first-term day count and activation date (C23), and the support-silence count (C21) — writing 'UNKNOWN — requires <source>' where a source is absent rather than omitting the row

Runs the onboarding gate before applying the renewal-window filter, so a first-term account past day 60 with no activation event appears in the assessment even though its renewal falls outside the 90-day window (C23)

evals.prompt: Acme's health score is 82 and they're renewing in six weeks. My gut says something is wrong. Can you check?
evals.expected_output: A single-account assessment that specifically tests the false-green mechanisms: buying-team usage separated from aggregate, champion liveness, override floors, and compound patterns. Should either confirm the green read with evidence or identify the masking.
assertions: Separates buying-team usage from aggregate usage and reports both
Explicitly checks champion liveness (bounce, directory, title, channel membership)
Evaluates every override floor and shows which fired with evidence
Tests all fourteen compound patterns, naming Buyer disconnect specifically
States what would change the assessment in 2-3 observable events
Marks any unavailable signal family as 'UNKNOWN — requires X' rather than treating it as clean, and caps confidence at what the Coverage Ledger permits
Names no customer-success-platform vendor anywhere in the output, referring to the category generically ('your CS platform', 'a CS platform's scorecard') when it needs to point at where a score lives

Reports acceptance latency, reschedule count over 90 days, and who actually accepted the last invitation as a named person and role — and scores the calendar before scoring anything said in the meetings (C22)
States the negotiation friction on the last close as contested, routine or frictionless, and does not treat an uncontested renewal as corroboration of the healthy score (C24)

evals.prompt: I only have CRM and billing data — no product analytics. Can you still tell me who's at risk?
evals.expected_output: A degraded but useful Low-confidence assessment with explicit renormalisation over the available families and a named blind spot — or, only under 40 percent coverage, a gap list instead of a score with the specific sources that would unlock it.
assertions: Degrades rather than refusing — still produces the commercial and billing family analysis in full
Computes coverage across the seven families and states the percentage
Renormalises weights over measured families rather than scoring missing families as zero risk
Caps confidence to Low or declares Insufficient, matching the stated criteria
Names which specific families are missing and what those gaps typically hide
Does not substitute an industry benchmark for the missing product-usage data
Records the reduced-coverage run and any defaulted weight profile in the Assumption Register

evals.prompt: Northwind just switched auto-renew off but everything else looks totally fine — usage is up, NPS is 9, no open tickets. Is this a false alarm?
evals.expected_output: The override floor must dominate. Score forced to Critical (85) regardless of the healthy weighted score, with the reasoning shown, plus the Exit preparation disconfirming test run before escalating.
assertions: Applies the auto-renew override floor and states that it overrides the weighted score
Shows both the weighted score and the post-floor score explicitly
Runs the disconfirming test — checks whether the change was our own re-papering — before escalating
Surfaces the contradiction between healthy usage/sentiment and the commercial action, and applies the stated tiebreak order
Recommends the Competitive re-bid play with owner and 24-hour verification step
Does not average the commercial signal against the healthy signals

Keeps the artifact internal — the risk score, band, ARR at risk, pattern name and play name appear in no customer-facing wording, and any outreach draft is delegated to the customer-voice standard rather than lifted from this document

evals.prompt: Good news for once — Zeta renewed early, no pushback at all, signed the same order form we sent. They've been quiet all year, barely any tickets, and I haven't had a meeting with their VP since March. Can you close them out as retained and tell me where to upsell?
evals.expected_output: A refusal to read the easy renewal as health. The account is scored as a Frictionless renewal on a low-engagement base: banded no lower than Watch, the pattern named, a next-cycle risk record opened at signature, the zero-ticket year scored as disengagement rather than stability, and the expansion ask withheld under the health gate with the withholding printed.
assertions: Names the Frictionless renewal compound pattern and states that zero negotiation events on a low-engagement account is a risk combination, not a clean outcome (C24)
Does not band the account Secure — the frictionless band floor of Watch is applied and stated, with the weighted score and the post-floor score both shown
Scores the near-zero ticket volume as risk (U-shaped support sub-score, 40 not 0) rather than as a stable account, and tests the Quiet quit pattern before accepting the quiet as resolution (C21)
Fills the negotiation-friction field explicitly as 'frictionless' and the calendar three-tuple, rather than omitting them because the renewal already closed
Refuses the upsell request and prints the withholding with its rule number (R8), rather than silently dropping it
Recommends the Engagement proof play with an owner and a date — one economic-buyer meeting inside 60 days whose purpose is that the buyer states the objective and the number
Opens a risk record for the next renewal dated from the signature, not from T-180 of the next cycle

evals.prompt: Don't worry about Epsilon, they're only three months in and their renewal isn't until next June. Just give me the accounts renewing this quarter.
evals.expected_output: The renewal-window scope is honoured, but the onboarding gate runs first and pulls Epsilon in anyway: day 94 of the first term with the activation event never fired fires Failed launch now, not at T-90. The renewal plan for that account is withheld and an implementation restart is recommended instead.
assertions: Runs the onboarding gate before the renewal-window filter and includes the first-term account despite its renewal falling outside the requested window (C23)
Prints days since contract start and the activation event as a date or the literal NEVER for every first-term account
Fires the Failed launch pattern at the day-60 gate rather than deferring it to the renewal window, and says so explicitly
Refuses to write a renewal plan for the account whose activation event has never fired, prints 'Renewal plan status: withheld', and names the milestone that unlocks it (C23)
Recommends the Implementation restart play with a re-baselined date, a written mutual commitment, an owner and a date — not a renewal-prep handoff
Still returns the requested this-quarter renewal list; the gate adds an account rather than replacing the answer

evals.prompt: Northwind's usage is fine and the last QBR went well, everyone was positive. Their VP has moved our monthly twice now and sent his analyst instead the time before. Am I overthinking it?
evals.expected_output: The calendar fires independently of usage. Two consecutive reschedules by the economic buyer applies the 60 floor regardless of the healthy usage read, acceptance latency and who-accepts are scored, and the recommended action is the calendar escalation within five working days.
assertions: Applies the two-consecutive-buyer-reschedules floor of 60 and states explicitly that it fires with no usage decline required and that healthy usage does not offset it (C22)
Scores and prints all three calendar fields — acceptance latency against the account's own baseline, reschedule count over 90 days, and who accepts, named with their role
Treats acceptance delegated to an analyst outside the buying centre as a scored withdrawal signal rather than as attendance
Weights the calendar record above the positive QBR sentiment and names the tiebreak rule it applied
Runs the innocent explanations first — leave, quarter-end, an assistant now triaging — before escalating
Recommends the Calendar escalation play: the third invitation comes from a VP with a specific reason to attend, inside five working days, with the failure condition named
